chain.title: CDOT Standard Plans for Traffic Controls for Highway Construction (latest editions) — first city in the corpus to adopt them wholesale for municipal work

min_lane_width_ft.note: LEDS §131: 'minimum of ten (10) feet unless otherwise authorized'. Flagger-closure templates require 12 ft — render 12 ft on flagger configurations (conservative).

conflict.label: minimum travel lane width
conflict.rendered: 10 ft general; 12 ft on flagger closures

sources.value: Minimum 12 ft travel lane must be maintained at all times

conflict.verdict: Both current, both Littleton. Plausible reconciliation (flagger closures carry two-way traffic through one lane) not adopted; render 10 ft general, 12 ft on flagger configurations.

device_spacing.rule: Cone spacing 25 ft flat on templates — no taper/tangent split stated.

sign_spacing.note: 'Approx. 100 ft, low-speed local streets (<35 mph)' — three-flagger template. Consistent with the regional 30/35 breakpoint family.

Approximate; intersection lane closure and full closure templates. Lower than the Aurora/Lakewood/Englewood 350 — recorded as published, not harmonized; LEDS defers to MUTCD/CDOT plans for what templates don't cover.

taper.rule: Taper 100 ft max on flagger closures (templates).

other.rule: Lane clearance >=5 ft from an open excavation and >=2 ft from curb/vertical obstruction; barricades mandatory if the 5-ft clearance fails.

geometry.note: Street closures are organized by flagger count (One/Two/Three Flagger Closure) — the only personnel-taxonomized template set in the corpus; a direct labor-quantity lookup per closure type.

deltas.rule: Provide flaggers and UTC when required — AFADs are not accepted (first AFAD ban in the corpus; adjacent Centennial, in otherwise-copied text, permits them at discretion).
Traffic cones are daytime-only. Lighted barricades for all overnight work — steady burn for delineation/channelization, flashing to denote a specific hazard.

effect.note: replaces cones on any overnight deployment

deltas.rule: Construction limited to one-half the roadway at any time unless the TCP approves otherwise; intersection/alley/driveway access maintained at all times (intersection closure only with City Engineer approval, minimum duration).

Steel plates are not to be utilized from September through May unless specifically approved by the City Engineer — a nine-month plate ban, the longest seasonal device rule in the corpus. Plates PE-designed, >=1 ft past trench edges, feathered.

trigger.condition: steel plate use, September through May

deltas.rule: An accessible pedestrian and bicycle route, per MUTCD standards, shall be maintained adjacent to the work area at all times; pedestrians shall not be diverted onto the roadway unless a detour route has been previously approved on the TCP. Spoils: >=4 ft of sidewalk kept clear.

TC removed within 48 hours of completion or the City corrects per Code 8-1-3. Existing pavement markings completely removed (black-out painting rejected); contractor installs, removes, and reinstates permanent markings.

hours.override_note: No work, cleanup, set-up, or other work-related activity outside these hours without Public Works Director authorization. No work Saturday, Sunday, or City/Federal holidays without written approval (holiday list enumerated, incl. Juneteenth and Day After Thanksgiving); contractor pays after-hours fees.

personnel.rule: Flaggers must hold proof of ACTIVE certification from a CDOT-accepted program (or as approved by the Traffic Engineer); MUTCD flagging procedures; orange/optic-yellow, reflectorized at night. No TCS-certification requirement anywhere in LEDS — the personnel gate is flagger-level.

UTC SHALL be used whenever normal traffic-signal operation is interrupted; UTC may be required on arterial/collector jobs per the City Engineer; contractor bears the cost. Cleanest UTC trigger in the corpus.

devices.rule: Retro-reflective faces; barricades painted/clean/weighted; damaged faces replaced. Temporary pavement markings at City Engineer discretion.

No-parking signs >=24 hrs ahead with prescribed wording ('No parking anytime TOW AWAY ZONE at all times' / limited-hours variant); sign spacing 20-25 ft. Full closure: Type III barricades, ROAD CLOSED + DETOUR signing at 200-ft spacing.

hazards.rule: Work without required permitting: $250 non-compliance fee, first offense (escalation implied, unspecified); waived if the City Engineer determines the work was emergency (broken water lines, blocked sewer services qualify).

notes.rule: Job-specific TCP prepared by the Contractor, reviewed by the City Engineer per a TCP Checklist; no work without an approved TCP; changes approved in writing before implementation; non-compliance -> Stop Work Order. TTC in the field is 'accepted by the Municipal Inspector' — inspector-level acceptance.
City Contractor's License required (eTRAKiT); the license taxonomy includes a dedicated Municipal ROW class (ICC Class M exam, $400). Bonds + insurance required for licensure; amounts not published.

source.doc: Littleton ROW Permits page + Development Application Fees (Res. 105-2025)

notes.rule: Pre-construction meeting, where staff requires one, is a hard gate — no permit until completed. Permit fees = unit rates on the annual Fee Schedule, cumulative, paid in full before issuance; the per-unit ROW excavation rates are not published on either fee page (surfaced per-application inside eTRAKiT).
Development-review resubmittals: all fees based on three rounds of review; 4th review = 50% of initial fees; 5th+ = 25% each (Res. 105-2025).

multi_agency.rule: Notify/coordinate utility companies, RTD, and CDOT; fire department approval for temporary surfaces; MHFD Criteria Manual Vol. 3 governs BMPs; Arapahoe County Open Space Tax (.00125 x valuation) collected on city permits.

items.label: After-hours inspection
items.note: 2-hour minimum, added to the permit, payable within 48 hrs.

items.label: ICC Test — Class M (Municipal ROW contractor license)

fees.note: Per-unit ROW excavation rates (LEDS §149's 'annual Fee Schedule') did not appear on either published fee page — Q-LIT-4 residual.

meters.note: Non-compliance fee, first offense; escalation implied, unspecified. Building-division scheme is separate: investigation (work without a building permit) = double the permit fee.

leads.label: Inspection requests (eTRAKiT)
leads.note: By 11:59 p.m. the prior business day; no same-day. After-hours inspections >=48 hrs by email.

leads.label: TC removal after completion
leads.note: Else the City corrects per Code 8-1-3.

notices.rule: Inform occupants of access limitations; driveway closures coordinated with owners, City Engineer final approval.
No-parking signs posted >=24 hrs ahead with prescribed TOW AWAY ZONE wording.

items.rule: Signed TCP kept at the work area during work hours; available to City or State inspection.
